stem: Why do green plants need sunlight? Answer in one or two sentences.
points: Plants make their own food (glucose) by photosynthesis
Light provides the energy needed for photosynthesis
model_answer: Plants need sunlight for photosynthesis: chlorophyll in the leaves absorbs light energy and uses it to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose (food) and oxygen.

stem: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours. Calculate its average speed. Show your working.
points: Uses average speed = distance ÷ time
Average speed = 60 km/h
model_answer: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 120 km ÷ 2 h = 60 km/h.

stem: What is the difference between a physical change and a chemical change? Give one example of each.
points: In a physical change no new substance is formed
In a chemical change a new substance is formed
Gives a correct example of each (e.g. melting ice; burning paper)
model_answer: A physical change does not form a new substance; only the state or shape changes, e.g. ice melting. A chemical change forms new substances with new properties, e.g. burning paper produces ash and gases.

stem: Explain why we have day and night on Earth.
points: The Earth rotates (spins) on its axis
One complete rotation takes about 24 hours
The side facing the Sun has day and the side facing away has night
model_answer: The Earth rotates on its axis once about every 24 hours. The half facing the Sun is lit and has day; the half facing away is dark and has night.

stem: A metal block has a mass of 200 g and a volume of 50 cm³. Calculate its density and say whether it will float or sink in water. Explain your answer.
points: Uses density = mass ÷ volume
Density = 4 g/cm³
It sinks because its density is greater than that of water (1 g/cm³)
model_answer: Density = mass ÷ volume = 200 g ÷ 50 cm³ = 4 g/cm³. Water's density is 1 g/cm³, so the block is denser than water and sinks.

stem: What is the job of red blood cells, and why is it useful that they have no nucleus?
points: They carry oxygen from the lungs to body cells
They contain haemoglobin, which combines with oxygen
Having no nucleus leaves more space for haemoglobin, so they carry more oxygen
model_answer: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the body cells. They contain haemoglobin, which combines with oxygen. With no nucleus there is more room for haemoglobin, so each cell carries more oxygen.

stem: Iron gates in Alexandria rust faster than iron gates in Aswan. Explain why.
points: Rusting needs iron, oxygen and water
The air in Alexandria is more humid (more water vapour)
Salt from the sea speeds up rusting
model_answer: Rusting happens when iron reacts with oxygen and water. Alexandria is on the coast, so its air is humid and also carries sea salt, which speeds up rusting. Aswan's air is dry.

stem: A metal spoon and a wooden spoon have been on the same table all day. The metal spoon feels colder when you touch it. Explain why.
points: Both spoons are actually at the same (room) temperature
Metal is a good conductor of heat; wood is a poor conductor (insulator)
The metal conducts heat away from the hand quickly, so it feels colder
model_answer: Both spoons are at room temperature. Metal is a good conductor of heat and wood is an insulator, so the metal takes heat from your hand quickly and feels colder.

stem: Why is the soil of the Nile Delta very fertile?
points: The Nile deposited silt in the Delta (during floods)
Silt is rich in minerals/nutrients that plants need
model_answer: For thousands of years the Nile flood carried silt and deposited it in the Delta. Silt is rich in minerals and nutrients, so crops grow well.

stem: Why does a person breathe faster when running?
points: The muscles need more energy when running
This energy comes from respiration, which uses oxygen
Faster breathing also removes the extra carbon dioxide produced
model_answer: Working muscles need more energy, which comes from respiration (glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy). Breathing faster takes in more oxygen and removes the extra carbon dioxide.

stem: Water in a kettle is heated from 25 °C until it reaches 100 °C. What is the change in temperature? What happens if you keep heating it? Explain.
points: Temperature change = 75 °C
The water boils at 100 °C
The temperature stays at 100 °C while boiling because the energy is used to change liquid to gas
model_answer: Change = 100 °C − 25 °C = 75 °C. At 100 °C the water boils; with more heating the temperature stays at 100 °C because the energy changes the water to steam rather than raising its temperature.

stem: Explain why salt water is a mixture and not a compound.
points: Salt and water are not chemically combined (no new substance forms)
They can be separated by a physical method such as evaporation
The proportions are not fixed (you can dissolve more or less salt)
model_answer: Salt water is a mixture because the salt and water are not chemically combined, so no new substance forms. They can be separated by evaporation, and the amount of salt can vary, unlike a compound with a fixed composition.

stem: During a storm we see lightning before we hear thunder. Why?
points: Lightning and thunder are produced at the same time
Light travels much faster than sound
model_answer: Lightning and thunder happen at the same moment, but light travels much faster (about 300 000 km/s) than sound (about 340 m/s), so the light reaches us first.

stem: A box weighing 600 N rests on an area of 2 m². Calculate the pressure it exerts. Then explain why a camel's wide feet help it walk on sand.
points: Uses pressure = force ÷ area
Pressure = 300 Pa (N/m²)
Wide feet spread the weight over a larger area, so the pressure on the sand is smaller
model_answer: Pressure = force ÷ area = 600 N ÷ 2 m² = 300 Pa. A camel's wide feet spread its weight over a large area, so the pressure is low and the feet do not sink into the sand.

stem: Why are bees important for flowering plants?
points: Bees carry pollen from one flower to another (pollination)
This lets the flower be fertilised and make seeds and fruits
The seeds can grow into new plants, so the plants reproduce
model_answer: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, which is called pollination. This lets the flowers be fertilised and make seeds and fruits, and the seeds grow into new plants.

stem: Explain the process of photosynthesis and why it is important for life on Earth. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Plants take in carbon dioxide (from air) and water (from soil)
Chlorophyll absorbs light energy
Glucose and oxygen are produced
Animals and humans depend on the oxygen and the food made by plants
model_answer: Photosynthesis is how green plants make their food. They take in carbon dioxide through their leaves and water through their roots. Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs light energy, which is used to turn these into glucose and oxygen. The glucose is food for the plant and is stored as starch. Oxygen is released into the air. Animals and humans breathe this oxygen and depend on plants for food, directly or through food chains, so photosynthesis supports almost all life on Earth.

stem: Describe the water cycle and explain how water moves around the Earth. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: The Sun heats water in seas, rivers and lakes and it evaporates
Water vapour rises, cools and condenses to form clouds
Water falls back as precipitation (rain, hail, snow)
Water collects in rivers, lakes and seas (or soaks into the ground) and the cycle repeats
model_answer: The Sun heats water in seas, rivers and lakes, and it evaporates into water vapour. The vapour rises, cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. When the droplets join and become heavy, they fall as precipitation such as rain. The water runs into rivers and seas or soaks into the ground, and then the cycle starts again.

stem: Explain how burning fossil fuels harms the environment and suggest one way to reduce the harm. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide
Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that traps heat, causing global warming
Other pollutants (e.g. sulfur dioxide, smoke) cause acid rain or air pollution/smog
Suggests a valid solution such as renewable energy (solar, wind)
model_answer: When coal, oil and natural gas burn, they release carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas: it traps heat in the atmosphere and causes global warming. Burning fuels also gives out sulfur dioxide and smoke, which cause acid rain and smog that harm our lungs and buildings. One solution is to use renewable energy such as solar power, like the Benban solar park in Aswan.

stem: Explain how a simple electric circuit makes a lamp light up. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: The circuit must be complete (closed) with no gaps
The battery (cell) provides the energy that pushes the current
Current flows through conducting wires and the lamp
A switch opens or closes the circuit to turn the lamp off or on
model_answer: A simple circuit has a battery, wires, a switch and a lamp. The battery gives energy and pushes the electric current around the circuit. The current flows through the metal wires, which are conductors, and through the lamp's filament, which glows. The circuit must be closed with no gaps. When the switch is open, the circuit is broken and the lamp goes off.

stem: A bus travels 220 km from Cairo to Alexandria in 2.75 hours. Calculate its average speed, and explain why the speedometer reading during the trip is often different from this value. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Uses average speed = total distance ÷ total time
Average speed = 80 km/h
The speedometer shows the instantaneous speed at one moment
The bus's speed changes during the trip (traffic, stops), so it is sometimes faster and sometimes slower than the average
model_answer: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 220 km ÷ 2.75 h = 80 km/h. The speedometer shows the instantaneous speed, the speed at one moment. During the trip the bus speeds up on the open road and slows down or stops in traffic and at toll gates. So at some moments it goes faster than 80 km/h and at others slower; 80 km/h is only the average over the whole journey.

stem: Describe a food chain in the River Nile and explain what could happen if one type of fish disappeared. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Producers (plants/algae) make their own food using sunlight
Food/energy passes from producers to consumers along the chain (gives a correct chain)
Animals that eat the fish would decrease or starve
Organisms the fish ate would increase in number
model_answer: In the Nile, algae and water plants are producers: they make their own food by photosynthesis. Small fish such as tilapia eat the algae, and herons or Nile perch eat the small fish, so energy passes along the chain: algae → tilapia → heron. If tilapia disappeared, the herons would lose food and their numbers would fall. The algae would no longer be eaten and would increase a lot. So removing one organism affects the whole chain.

stem: Explain how earthquakes happen and why some countries have more earthquakes than others. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: The Earth's crust is broken into large tectonic plates
The plates move slowly (pushed by currents in the mantle)
Stress builds up and is released suddenly, sending out seismic waves (shaking)
Most earthquakes happen near plate boundaries, so countries on boundaries have more
model_answer: The Earth's crust is broken into huge pieces called tectonic plates. They move slowly because of convection currents in the mantle. Where plates push, pull or slide past each other, they get stuck and stress builds up. When the rocks suddenly break or slip, energy is released as seismic waves and the ground shakes. Countries on plate boundaries, like Japan and Turkey, have many earthquakes, while countries far from boundaries have fewer.

stem: Explain the differences between acids and bases, how we can test for them, and what happens when they react together. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Acids have pH below 7 and bases (alkalis) have pH above 7
An indicator changes colour: acids turn blue litmus red, bases turn red litmus blue
Neutralisation: acid + base → salt + water
Gives a correct everyday use of neutralisation (e.g. antacid for stomach acid)
model_answer: Acids have a pH below 7 and taste sour, while bases have a pH above 7; pure water is neutral at 7. We test with an indicator: acids turn blue litmus red and bases turn red litmus blue. When an acid reacts with a base, they neutralise each other and form a salt and water. For example, an antacid tablet neutralises extra hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

stem: Explain how the human body defends itself against disease-causing germs. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: The skin (and mucus) acts as a barrier that stops germs entering
White blood cells engulf and destroy germs
The body makes antibodies against specific germs
Vaccines (weakened/dead germs) make the body produce antibodies/memory, giving immunity
model_answer: The skin is a barrier that stops most germs from entering, and mucus in the nose traps germs. If germs get in, some white blood cells engulf and digest them. Other white blood cells make antibodies that attach to a specific germ and help destroy it. Vaccines contain weakened or dead germs, so the body makes antibodies and memory cells without getting ill, and next time it can fight the real germ quickly.

stem: Ahmed wants to find the density of a small stone with a mass of 300 g. He puts water in a measuring cylinder up to 50 mL, then drops the stone in and the water rises to 150 mL. Explain how he finds the density and whether the stone floats or sinks. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Volume of the stone = 150 − 50 = 100 mL (100 cm³), found by displacement
Uses density = mass ÷ volume
Density = 3 g/cm³
The stone sinks because its density is greater than water's (1 g/cm³)
model_answer: The stone pushes away (displaces) water equal to its own volume, so its volume is 150 mL − 50 mL = 100 mL = 100 cm³. Density = mass ÷ volume = 300 g ÷ 100 cm³ = 3 g/cm³. Water has a density of 1 g/cm³. Because the stone is denser than water, it sinks.

stem: Explain why the Moon seems to change its shape during the month (the phases of the Moon). Write 4-8 sentences.
points: The Moon does not make light; it reflects light from the Sun
The Moon orbits the Earth about once a month (about 29.5 days)
Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun
As the Moon orbits, we see different amounts of the lit half, giving phases (new, crescent, full)
model_answer: The Moon does not produce its own light; it reflects sunlight. One half of the Moon always faces the Sun and is lit. The Moon orbits the Earth about every 29.5 days, so we see the lit half from different angles. At new moon we see almost none of it, then a crescent, then a half and at full moon the whole lit side; then it shrinks again. The Earth's shadow does not cause the phases.

stem: You have a mixture of sand, salt and water. Explain how to separate it to get back the sand, the salt and the water. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Salt dissolves in water but sand does not
Filtration separates the sand (left on the filter paper)
Evaporating/heating the filtrate leaves the salt
Distillation (condensing the vapour) collects the pure water
model_answer: Salt dissolves in water but sand does not. First we filter the mixture: the sand stays on the filter paper as the residue and the salt solution passes through. Then we heat the salt solution in a distillation apparatus: the water boils, the steam is cooled in the condenser and collected as pure water, and the salt is left behind as crystals.

stem: A large steel ship floats, but a small steel nail sinks. Explain why. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Weight acts downwards and upthrust (buoyancy) acts upwards
An object floats when the upthrust equals its weight
Upthrust equals the weight of water displaced; the ship's shape displaces a large volume of water
The ship's average density (steel plus air inside) is less than water's; the nail is denser than water
model_answer: Two forces act on an object in water: its weight downwards and upthrust upwards. An object floats when the upthrust is equal to its weight. Upthrust equals the weight of water the object displaces. The ship is hollow, so its shape displaces a huge volume of water, giving a large upthrust. Because it is full of air, its average density is less than that of water. A solid nail displaces very little water and is denser than water, so it sinks.

stem: Explain why children look like their parents but are not exactly the same as them or as their brothers and sisters. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: Traits are controlled by genes, found on chromosomes (made of DNA) in the nucleus
A child receives half of its chromosomes/genes from each parent (through the egg and sperm)
Some genes are dominant and some are recessive, so a trait can be hidden
Different combinations of genes cause variation, so siblings differ
model_answer: Features such as eye colour are controlled by genes, which are parts of DNA on the chromosomes in the nucleus. A child gets half of its chromosomes from the mother's egg and half from the father's sperm, so it looks like both parents. Some genes are dominant and hide recessive ones, so a child may show a trait that neither parent shows. Each egg and sperm carries a different mix of genes, so brothers and sisters get different combinations, which causes variation.

stem: Mona heats crushed ice and records the temperature every minute: −10 °C, −4 °C, 0 °C, 0 °C, 0 °C, 6 °C, 13 °C, 20 °C. Describe and explain her results. Write 4-8 sentences.
points: The temperature rises from −10 °C to 0 °C as the solid ice warms
The temperature stays at 0 °C while the ice melts
During melting the energy is used to change state (separate the particles), not to raise the temperature
After all the ice has melted, the temperature of the water rises again (to 20 °C)
model_answer: At first the temperature of the ice rises from −10 °C to 0 °C. It then stays at 0 °C for about three minutes while the ice melts. During melting the heat energy is used to overcome the forces between the particles and change the solid into a liquid, so the temperature does not rise. When all the ice has melted, the energy warms the water and the temperature rises again to 20 °C.
